description: The bearish mirror of FVG registration: the gap is measured downward, and the band is built from the opposite pair of extremes.
labelling_rationale: SLS §5.4 states the bullish rule and says 'mirror bearish'. Mirrored, a bearish gap exists when H[c3] < L[c1], the zone is [H[c3], L[c1]] rather than [H[c1], L[c3]], and Consequent Encroachment remains the midpoint. Candle 0 lows at 109 and candle 2 highs at 105, so the gap is 4 and the zone is [105, 109] with CE at 107, confirmed at the close of candle 2. The registration filter is the same 0.25 x ATR: true ranges for candles 0..2 are 2, 11 and 8, summing to 21 over three candles for an ATR of exactly 7 and a floor of 1.75, which a gap of 4 clears on size alone, so displacement is not needed — and could not apply, since §5.10 needs a 20-candle lookback this series lacks. Nothing follows candle 2, so no lifecycle transition can occur and the zone remains OPEN, which is not a terminal state and therefore counts as one live zone. This case exists because a mirrored detector is a classic place for an inverted comparison to hide: getting the bullish path right proves nothing about the bearish one, and the band being built from the OTHER two extremes is exactly the kind of detail a copy-paste mirror gets wrong. Candle numbers above are scenario-relative; the 297 declared filler candles (SLS §1.9 warm-up) shift them by 297 in the expected output. The filler's high matches the scenario's first candle so the seam cannot form a swing high, and its low sits below so it cannot form a swing low; neither a bullish nor a bearish three-candle gap spans the seam, so declared history registers no zone of its own. Extended 2026-08-23 when the harness began running the OTE, order-block and interaction passes alongside the FVG pass, in the pipeline's own order. The added counts follow SLS 5.9's grammar table: a Touch is any candle whose range intersects the band; a Rejection is a touch that closes outside on the polarity side with a wick of at least 0.3 x ATR into the zone; a Mitigation is reaching half the zone depth and closing outside on the polarity side; and a Respect is 'Rejection or Mitigation without any close-through', which is why respects track them rather than adding a third event. Dealing ranges and order blocks are zero throughout: 5.7 needs confirmed external swings that these short scenarios never produce, and 5.1's qualification reads S4/S5 evidence that a zone-only dataset does not generate.
